name: Blog Layout (List and Post)
description: A blog's list page and post page: post cards whose title link covers the card, an article with underlined links and code that scrolls inside itself, pagination that marks the current page, and sharing without third-party scripts.

tokens.note: Suggested defaults for a project without a design. The project's design tokens and existing components win.

layout.layering: Layers, bottom to top: the page, sticky bars, dropdowns and popovers, toasts, then modals, which make the rest of the page inert. The project's layering scale wins; native <dialog> and the popover attribute use the top layer and need no z-index. A sticky header is a sticky bar; the menu is a modal.

positioningContract.header: Static or sticky at the top; scroll-padding-top at its height when it sticks
positioningContract.listPage: The cards in a grid, beside an optional sidebar from 1024 px
positioningContract.postPage: The article at its reading width, beside an optional sidebar from 1024 px
positioningContract.footer: At the end of the page, scrolling with it

invariants: The page scrolls, not a box inside it
Nothing scrolls sideways down to 320 px wide; code blocks scroll inside themselves
A sticky sidebar fits the window below the header, or scrolls inside itself
Every card is visible without script, under reduced motion, and when printing

aiAgentInstructions.summary: Build or extend a blog: the list page with post cards and pagination, and the post page with the article, sharing, comments, and related posts. A card is one link, its title, covering the card; links in the text are underlined; sharing needs no third-party scripts. The guide's colors, type, and shapes are a fallback for a project without a design of its own. Build on the project's templates, cards, and form components when it has suitable ones. Implement only what the task needs, keep existing APIs, and match the project's styling and tokens. The project's conventions win for styling and visual defaults; if one conflicts with an accessibility or correctness requirement in this guide, ask the user instead of choosing silently. Target WCAG 2.2 AA.
keyFeatures: Post cards whose title link covers the card, with other links raised above it
An article at a reading width, with underlined links, code that scrolls inside itself, and dates as time elements
Pagination with aria-current="page" and no links that pretend to be disabled
Share links without third-party scripts, and a Copy link button that says whether it worked
Comments rendered as text, and forms with visible labels and one status region
A fallback look with a neutral accent, used only when the project has no design of its own
implementationSteps: 1. Detect the framework and its version, the styling system, the tokens, the content source (a CMS, Markdown files), and the existing components (projectDetection). If the project already has blog templates or a theme, configure or extend them to meet this guide instead of building others, and keep their APIs.
2. Choose what the task needs: the list page, the post page, the sidebar, comments, the newsletter. Leave out the rest.
3. Lay out the pages and their landmarks (structure, components.ListPage, components.PostPage).
4. Build the post cards (frameworkPatterns.postCard) and the pagination (components.Pagination).
5. Build the article (components.Article) and the sharing (frameworkPatterns.copyLink, implementationDetails.sharing).
6. Add the comments and the newsletter if the task asks for them (implementationDetails.comments, implementationDetails.newsletter).
7. Use the project's styles; only without a design of its own, use designSystem as the fallback.
8. Check the result against testingChecklist with a keyboard, a screen reader, a phone, 200% zoom, and reduced motion, and run the project's existing tests and checks.

Header.description: The site's header, with the skip link

Main.description: main#main: the article (its header with the h1, the body), share links, comments, related posts

Sidebar.description: Optional aside: the table of contents, the author's bio, related posts

StatusRegion.description: One polite status region per page, present from the start

ListPage.description: **The list page**: the header, an optional hero with the blog's title, the post cards, an optional sidebar, the pagination, and the footer. The blog's title is the page's <h1>, and each card's title an <h2>.

behavior.layout: One column of cards below 768 px, two from 768 px; from 1024 px, two beside a sidebar, or three without one, since three beside a 320 px sidebar leaves cards about 240 px wide.

PostPage.description: **The post page**: the header, the post in an <article> (its title as the page's <h1>, the author, the date, the reading time, and an optional image), share links, comments, related posts, and the footer. Comments and related posts are sections with an <h2>, and a related post's card title is an <h3>.

behavior.header: The post's header can span the page's width; the body stays at its reading width.

PostCard.description: The card's title link covers the whole card, so a click anywhere follows it, while the card stays one link named by its title. Making the whole card an <a> would read the card's text as the link's name, and the category and author links inside it would be nested links.

behavior.innerLinks: Other links in the card (a category, an author) sit above the cover, and still work (checked in Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit). The trade-off: the excerpt's text can't be selected.
behavior.image: The image is decorative (alt=""), since the title names the link. Images in the first screen load at once, the featured one with fetchpriority="high"; the rest can be loading="lazy". Every image has width and height.
behavior.text: Titles wrap; nothing is cut off with an ellipsis. An excerpt may be clamped to two or three lines, since the post is a click away.
behavior.meta: The date is a <time datetime="2026-10-01">, and the meta line reads in a sensible order: category, date, reading time.
behavior.focusAndHover: The focus ring goes around the whole card, and a hover changes the shadow; under reduced motion, cards don't move.

Article.description: The body is 16 to 18 px with a line height of 1.6 to 1.8, at most about 70 characters a line (720 px). Headings go <h2> to <h4> in order.

behavior.links: Links in the text are underlined. Without an underline, a link's color needs 3:1 against the text around it and another cue on hover and focus (WCAG 1.4.1); the safe default is the underline.
behavior.images: Images have alt text that says what they show; an image with a caption is a <figure> with a <figcaption>.
behavior.code: A code block scrolls sideways inside itself, never the page. A block that scrolls gets tabindex="0", so the keyboard can scroll it, and sits in a <figure> whose caption names it, as the Documentation guide shows.
behavior.tableOfContents: A post has a table of contents only if it's long; the Documentation guide covers one that marks the section being read.

Sidebar.description: On the list page: categories, tags, search, and the newsletter. Search is a labelled field in a <search> element (or a form with role="search"), so it's a landmark. On the post page: the table of contents, the author's bio, and related posts.

behavior.sticky: Sticky is optional, and only if the sidebar fits the window below the sticky header; otherwise it scrolls inside itself (max-height the window's height minus the header's, overflow-y: auto), or its end can't be reached until the page ends.
behavior.smallScreens: From 1024 px it sits beside the posts, 280 to 320 px wide; below that it follows the content.

Pagination.description: A <nav aria-label="Pagination"> with a list of links. The current page is marked with aria-current="page" and looks different by more than color.

behavior.ends: Links can't be disabled, so there's no Previous link on the first page and no Next link on the last; show nothing, or plain text.
behavior.names: A page number's name includes the number it shows: "Page", visually hidden, then "2". On phones, Previous, "Page 2 of 8", and Next are enough.
behavior.urls: Each page has its own URL (/blog/page/2 or ?page=2), so pages can be shared and Back works.

Header.description: The site's header: a skip link, the logo, a <nav> labelled "Main", and the links that apply (Search, Subscribe). If it sticks, position: sticky and scroll-padding-top at its height keep focused elements clear of it (WCAG 2.2 2.4.11).

behavior.menu: Below 1024 px, the links move into a menu in a native <dialog>, as the Navigation Bar guide says.

desktop.list: Two columns of cards beside the sidebar, or three without one

tablet.list: Two columns of cards; the sidebar follows the content
tablet.post: The article; the sidebar follows it

mobile.post: The article at the window's width, with 16 px padding

resizeHandling.approach: CSS does the layout at every width; nothing listens to resize events.

menuOpen.description: Whether the menu dialog is open, below 1024 px.

formStatus.description: The newsletter's or the comment form's state.

ssrConsiderations.pages: Render the list and the post on the server; every link works before the script runs.
ssrConsiderations.dates: Render dates on the server in the reader's locale, or in one fixed format, so they don't change after hydration.

navigationBehavior.pagination: Each page has its own URL (/blog/page/2 or ?page=2), so pages can be shared and Back works.
navigationBehavior.onRouteChange: In a single-page app, update the title, move focus to the new page's h1 (tabindex="-1"), and close the menu.

screenReader.cards: The card's title link covers the whole card, so a click anywhere follows it, while the card stays one link named by its title. Making the whole card an <a> would read the card's text as the link's name, and the category and author links inside it would be nested links.
screenReader.sharing: Copy link copies the post's canonical address, not the one with tracking parameters. It says "Link copied" on the button for a moment and in the page's one status region, which is emptied first, so a second copy is announced too. The clipboard can refuse: navigator.clipboard.writeText was refused in Chromium without the clipboard permission and allowed after a click in Firefox and WebKit (checked), so a failure is said too.

implementationDetails.sharing: Share links are plain links to each site's share page (X, LinkedIn, Facebook, Mastodon), without the sites' scripts, which track readers. Each is named "Share on X", and says so when it opens a new tab. Copy link copies the post's canonical address, not the one with tracking parameters. It says "Link copied" on the button for a moment and in the page's one status region, which is emptied first, so a second copy is announced too. The clipboard can refuse: navigator.clipboard.writeText was refused in Chromium without the clipboard permission and allowed after a click in Firefox and WebKit (checked), so a failure is said too. navigator.share() opens the device's share sheet where it exists; feature-detect it, and keep the links for everyone else.
implementationDetails.comments: Comments are user content: render them as text, or as HTML sanitized on the server, never as raw HTML. The server handles spam and moderation. The form's fields have visible labels: name (autocomplete="name"), email (type="email", autocomplete="email"), and the comment. Errors and timing follow the Form Validation Pattern, and the result goes to the status region. An embedded comment service loads third-party scripts and tracking; say so, and ask before adding one.
implementationDetails.newsletter: The form says what people sign up for and how often they'll hear from you. The field has a visible label, type="email", and autocomplete="email"; the result ("Check your inbox to confirm") and errors go to the status region.
implementationDetails.motion: All motion is optional. The hero and the first cards are visible at load; they don't fade in from opacity 0, which would delay the largest image's paint. A scroll reveal, if any, hides only cards below the window when the script runs, on screens, when motion is allowed, as the Landing Page guide's does. Without script, under reduced motion, and when printing, nothing is hidden. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, card hovers change color or shadow only.
implementationDetails.layering: Layers, bottom to top: the page, sticky bars, dropdowns and popovers, toasts, then modals, which make the rest of the page inert. The project's layering scale wins; native <dialog> and the popover attribute use the top layer and need no z-index. A sticky header is a sticky bar; the menu is a modal.

framework.description: Find the framework, its version, and how existing components are written before writing code.
detectionSteps: Read the project's dependencies (package.json or its equivalent) for the framework and its version, and use the syntax that version supports.
Open two or three existing components to see their file structure, state handling, and naming.
Look for an existing component that already does this job, in the project or in a design system or UI library it uses, and build on it.

stylingSystem.description: Use the styling system the project already uses, and only that one.
detectionSteps: Check the dependencies and config for the styling setup: Tailwind (version 4 keeps its theme in CSS with @theme, version 3 in tailwind.config.*), CSS Modules, Sass, CSS-in-JS, or plain CSS.
See how existing components apply styles and compose class names, for example with cn or clsx.
Check for design documentation: DESIGN.md, a design system package, or Storybook stories for existing components.
adaptationRules: Write styles the way existing components do, and add no new styling library or system.
With plain CSS, use classes in the project's stylesheets instead of inline styles, except for values computed at runtime.
If the setup is unclear or mixed, ask before choosing.

designTokens.description: Use the project's tokens for color, spacing, radius, type, shadows, motion, and layering.
detectionSteps: Find the tokens: CSS custom properties, a Tailwind theme (@theme or config), a theme object, or a tokens file.
Use them instead of this guide's example values; where there are none, match the closest existing components.
Check that the colors you use meet the contrast minimums: 4.5:1 for text, and 3:1 for focus indicators, icons, and control boundaries.

frameworkPatterns.note: Short snippets in plain HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for the parts that are easiest to get wrong; adapt them to the project's framework and its version. The header and its menu are in the Navigation Bar guide.

copyLink.description: Copy link: copies the canonical address, says "Link copied" on the button and in the page's status region (emptied first, so a second copy is announced too), and says when the clipboard refused.

edgeCases.noImage: The card keeps the same title, excerpt, and meta; leave the image's space out rather than showing an empty box.
edgeCases.longTitle: It wraps on every screen; nothing is cut off.
edgeCases.firstLastPage: No Previous link on the first page and no Next link on the last.
edgeCases.noComments: Say so in a sentence, with the form below it.
edgeCases.noScript: Every card is visible and every link works; only Copy link and the share sheet need the script.

must: Build on the project's templates, cards, and form components when they're suitable, and keep their APIs
Use the project's styles; only without a design of its own, use this guide's fallback values
Make each card one link, its title, and underline links in the text
Use the project's framework version, styling system, and tokens, the way existing components do
mustNot: Wrap a whole card in a link, or nest links
Add third-party share or comment scripts, or any dependency, without asking
Disable a pagination link; leave it out instead
Cut titles off with an ellipsis
Use inline styles for static values in a plain-CSS project, or hardcode colors the project has tokens for

testingChecklist: The list page and the post page each start with a skip link and have one h1; the post is an article, the sidebar an aside, and the pagination a nav
A post card is one link, its title, which covers the whole card; a category or author link inside it still works, and the focus ring goes around the card
Card images are decorative (alt="") when the title names the link; images in the first screen load at once, and every image has width and height
Card titles wrap instead of being cut off; only an excerpt may be clamped
Links in the article's text are underlined, and text meets 4.5:1
A code block scrolls sideways inside itself and can be reached with Tab, and the page never scrolls sideways at 320 px wide
Dates are time elements with a datetime attribute
Pagination marks the current page with aria-current="page", and has no Previous link on the first page or Next link on the last
Share links go to each site's share page without third-party scripts, and say so when they open a new tab
Copy link copies the post's address and says so in the status region, or says that copying failed; a second copy is announced too
Comments are rendered as text or sanitized HTML, never as raw HTML
The newsletter and comment forms have visible labels, and their results go to the status region
A sticky sidebar fits the window below the header, or scrolls inside itself
Without script, under reduced motion, and when printing, nothing is hidden, and cards don't move on hover under reduced motion
Styles come from the project's styling system and tokens; the guide's colors are only a fallback
